dedupe_keys.name: gb railway network model with topology and daily passenger flows itrc university of oxford

description: This open-source model represents the Great Britain railway network as a GIS network of nodes and edges and estimates daily passenger flows on it. The script rail_od_flows.py combines 2019 train timetables from ATOC, annual station usage estimates for 2017/18 from the Office of Rail and Road and the network to build a 24-hour origin-destination matrix of passenger trips, and assemble_flows.py aggregates the flows onto every node and edge. The network of stations and routes, the matches between ATOC, ORR and network identifiers and the outputs are the authors' own, cleaned from OpenStreetMap and Ordnance Survey open data. It was developed at the University of Oxford within ITRC, and users are asked to cite the vulnerability framework of Pant, Hall and Blainey (2016). Coverage is national (Great Britain). The Python code is free under the MIT licence and available in a GitHub repository, archived by Software Heritage (last change September 2023); the timetable must be downloaded separately from ATOC with a free account. Caveats: it needs Python 3.6, uses one year of timetables and station usage, and the failure analysis was still in progress. It supports network flow and cascading failure analysis of rail disruption, such as flood or asset failures on passenger trips. It complements the Network Rail open data feeds and is related to the SUMO simulator for rail operations.
